note: One statement a day for residents to agree or disagree with. Each comes from an open issue and is worded neutrally (rules in UPDATE.md). Only questions with status "approved" are shown. Results are what participants said, not what residents want.

questions.text: Portsmouth should keep the resident parking pilot (free parking for residents in pilot zones, paid parking for nonresidents) after its first year.
Portsmouth should create a separate stormwater fee to pay for managing rain runoff.
A covered stage at Prescott Park, paid for by the Prescott Park Arts Festival, would be good for the park.
The city should go ahead with the phased $58.6 million renovation of City Hall and the police station.
Portsmouth should keep the resident parking pilot, where residents with registered plates park free in zones near downtown and nonresidents pay, after its first year.
The Planning Board should move ahead with the zoning changes in the Housing Action Plan the City Council adopted in September.
The McIntyre Federal Building site at 62 Daniel Street should be redeveloped with the three new multi-story buildings the owner has proposed.
Portsmouth should work with the Prescott Park Arts Festival on a covered stage in Prescott Park paid for by the Festival.
Portsmouth should go ahead with the $20.1 million renovation of the Career and Technical Education Center that the capital plan schedules over the next six years.
The next capital plan should set aside more than the current $6.2 million for citywide storm drainage improvements.
